raw: {"description": "Hey team, I just submitted a claim for the new Dell XPS 13 I bought for my design work — it’s a company-approved model, and I used my personal card since I needed it urgently for the client pitch last week. The receipt is attached, and the total came to $487. It’s a brand-new laptop with a serial number, so it’s definitely equipment, not office supplies. I know it’s under $500, but I didn’t want to risk anything since it’s a high-value tool I’ll be using daily. I also included the original invoice showing the manufacturer's warranty, just in case. Let me know if you need anything else — it’s just standard gear for the job, and I’m happy to provide more details.", "category": "equipment", "routing": "needs_manager", "rationale": "Hardware under $500 with a receipt routes to needs_manager, as equipment is not an auto-approvable category and the purchase is under $500, despite being a necessary tool for work."}

{"description": "Hey team, just wanted to flag this dinner I had last night with the lead contact from the new Acme Corp project — we were finalizing the scope and timeline, and I figured it was a good chance to build rapport. It was at a nice little Italian place downtown, and the total came to $245, which includes a couple of bottles of wine (one was $65 alone, but the rest of the meal was solid). I’ve attached the receipt, and I made sure to note on the form that a client was present. I know it’s a bit over the $150 mark for client entertainment, and I’m not trying to game the system — just thought it was worth the investment in the relationship. The meal itself was just food and non-alcoholic drinks, but the wine was on the bill as part of the group order. I’ll double-check the receipt to see if the alcohol can be separated, but I’m not sure if that’s even necessary since the client was there and it’s a business dinner. Anyway, just submitting this for approval.", "category": "client_entertainment", "routing": "needs_finance", "rationale": "The claim involves client entertainment with a client present and exceeds $150, which routes to needs_finance per the expense policy's rules."}

{"description": "So, I’ve been using my personal MacBook for work stuff for months now, and it’s getting kind of slow—like, really slow. I finally had to upgrade to a new one, but I had to buy it out of pocket since the company’s not replacing laptops yet. I ended up getting a MacBook Pro with M3 chip, 16GB RAM, and 1TB SSD, which was $1,800. I attached the receipt and even kept the original box. It’s not like I’m trying to game the system—I just need something that can handle design work without freezing every 3 seconds. I know it’s over $500, but it’s not like I’m spending company money on a luxury device. It’s a work necessity at this point.", "category": "equipment", "routing": "needs_finance", "rationale": "Hardware at or over $500 routes to needs_finance, and this claim involves a personal device purchased for work use, which still qualifies as equipment under the policy."}

{"description": "Hey, so I was working remotely from my apartment last week and my old laptop finally gave up — screen went all pixelated and it wouldn’t boot up. I had to order a new one fast because I’m on a tight deadline for the client deliverables. Got a brand-new Dell XPS 15 with a 16GB RAM and 512GB SSD, and it came with a $500 monitor and a $90 docking station all in one package on the receipt. Total was $2,190. The invoice was in USD, and I bought it from the company’s approved vendor site, but I used my personal credit card since the company card was maxed out. I didn’t get a receipt from the vendor yet — just the email confirmation with the order total. But I know it’s legit because I can pull up the order history. The laptop has a serial number, so I know it’s not a consumable. Just wanted to get it approved before I forget to submit it. It’s a personal device I’m using for work, but I really need it to keep up with the sprint timeline.", "category": "equipment", "routing": "needs_finance", "rationale": "The claim is for equipment totaling over $500, and bundled purchases are judged by the receipt total, which exceeds $500, so it routes to needs_finance per the Equipment section of the Expense Software Policy."}

{"description": "I'm a remote worker and wanted to upgrade my home office setup for the team event next week — I bought a new ergonomic chair and a second monitor, both on the same receipt for $620 total. The chair is for long video calls, and the monitor will help me collaborate better with the team during the event. I didn’t realize the bundle would be over $500 — I just thought it was a reasonable upgrade to support remote work. The receipt is attached. Should this go to needs_finance? I'm confused because it's not travel or software, but I know equipment over $500 goes there. Is this still considered equipment even though it's for a team event?", "category": "equipment", "routing": "needs_finance", "rationale": "Bundled hardware purchases over $500 total route to needs_finance, as per the Equipment rule in the Software & Equipment Purchasing Policy."}

{"description": "Okay, so I'm really confused about this mileage claim — I drove my personal car for a client meeting in downtown Chicago last week, and I used my phone's GPS app to track the distance, which came out to 128 miles. I'm not sure if this counts as travel or if it's something else, and I also didn't get a receipt for anything because it was just fuel and wear-and-tear. I did use my personal car, which isn't company property, but I was doing work-related travel — the client is from Acme Corp, and we were discussing a design brief for their new product. I didn't have a receipt for the gas because I paid in cash, and I also didn't have a ticket or anything — just the mileage log on my phone. I think this should be reimbursed because I was on company business, but I'm not sure what category this falls under. Also, the trip was over $500 in total if you add up the fuel costs based on current gas prices, but I don't have a receipt for that either. I just don't know what to do. Should I submit it as travel? Or is it personal? I'm not even sure if mileage counts as travel — the policy says mileage is included in travel, but I didn't use a company vehicle, so is that a problem? I just want to be clear — I'm not trying to get anything free, but I did spend money and put in extra work. Also, I didn't submit this within 60 days — I waited because I thought I’d get a receipt from the gas station, but they didn’t have one. I’m really sorry about that. But it was a legitimate work trip. Should I just file it as office_supplies because it’s a personal expense? I don't know. Can I get this approved? I really need the reimbursement for the gas.", "category": "equipment", "routing": "needs_finance", "rationale": "The claim involves a personal device used for work (personal car), but the mileage expense itself is not a valid category; the confusion stems from misapplying personal vehicle costs to a claim category, and since the user is requesting reimbursement for a personal device expense under a non-applicable category, the routing defaults to needs_finance as per the policy's rule that personal items (like personal vehicles) are rejected unless approved through a proper equipment process, and this claim lacks a receipt, making

{"description": "Hey, I’m so confused about this expense I just submitted — it was for a bulk order of printer supplies that I thought was straightforward. I bought 12 reams of premium A4 paper, 24 packs of high-capacity ink cartridges, and 100 custom-designed sticky notes for the design team, all from the company’s approved vendor. The total came to $187.45, which is way over $75, and I have the receipt. I didn’t realize there was a $75 cap for auto-approval, but the stuff is all office supplies — paper, ink, small desk items under $50 apiece, and the sticky notes were only $0.95 each. I thought since it’s a bulk order and the individual items are under $50, and they’re all consumable, it should still count as office_supplies. But now I’m not sure if I should have broken it into separate claims or if it’s automatically going to be rejected just because it’s over $75. Also, I’m not sure why I can’t just auto-approve it like I did with the $45 bottle of printer ink last month — that was approved in auto_approve. This feels like a gray area. Is this even considered a single claim or should I split it? I really need to get these materials for the client pitch this week, and I don’t want to mess up the approval process. Can someone clarify what happens if the total is over $75 but all items are consumable and under $50 each? The receipt is attached, and I didn’t miss anything. I just don’t understand why I can’t get this through quickly.", "category": "office_supplies", "routing": "needs_manager", "rationale": "All office supplies over $75 route to needs_manager, as auto_approve only applies to claims under $75, regardless of item type or receipt."}

{"description": "Hey, I'm really confused about this whole expense thing — I bought a new external hard drive for my work laptop because the old one crashed during a client demo, and I didn’t think I needed to keep the receipt since it was under $500, but now I’m being told I need to submit it? It was like $485, and the receipt is probably in my email inbox somewhere, but I can’t find it right now. I just want to make sure I’m not messing up the process. It’s not like it’s a fancy thing — it’s just a standard 2TB portable drive, no serial number on the label, but it’s for work use only, definitely not personal. I was thinking it might be office supplies since it’s a peripheral, but then I remembered the policy says accessories with serial numbers are equipment, but this one didn’t have one printed on it? I’m not sure. I just need to get this reimbursed so I can replace it before the next project — my manager’s gonna be mad if I don’t have backup storage for the data. Do I even need a receipt? The vendor was a local tech shop, not online. I swear I paid cash, but I don’t have anything to prove it. I don’t want to get flagged or rejected, but I’m not sure what the right category is — it’s not software, not travel, not meals. It’s just a hard drive, right? But the policy says anything with a serial number is equipment, and I’m not even sure if it has one. I’m so lost.", "category": "equipment", "routing": "needs_manager", "rationale": "Hardware under $500 with a receipt routes to needs_manager, but this claim lacks a receipt, so it defaults to needs_manager per the routing policy’s rule that missing receipts send claims to needs_manager regardless of amount."}

{"description": "As a remote worker based in Austin, I am ordering a bulk supply of ergonomic office accessories to support my home workspace setup, which has become essential for maintaining productivity during extended work hours. The order consists of 12 high-quality, replaceable pen refills (each under $5 in cost), 15 desk organizers (under $25 per unit, consumable in nature), and 20 wireless charging pads (each under $40, intended for desk use). All items are branded as 'office supplies' and are purchased directly from a corporate supplier via a company-provided procurement portal. The total cost of the order is $628.20, which includes shipping and handling. Although the order is for personal workspace optimization, I am submitting it for reimbursement under the company's remote worker stipend program. The receipt is attached, and all items are intended for professional use. However, two of the wireless charging pads were purchased for use in my personal living space, where I occasionally work from a side table, and the pen refills were ordered in a quantity larger than needed for my current workload. Given the volume and nature of the order, I am seeking clarity on whether this qualifies for reimbursement.", "category": "office_supplies", "routing": "needs_manager", "rationale": "The claim qualifies as office_supplies because it consists of consumable desk items (pen refills, desk organizers) and accessories under $50, and although the total exceeds $75, the claim is not auto-approvable due to the bulk quantity and mixed personal/professional use, which triggers the needs_manager queue per the routing policy."}

{"description": "Okay, so I’m a remote worker, and I’ve been working from home for the past few months, but I finally got to the point where I need a proper setup. I ordered this new high-end 27-inch monitor and a USB-C docking station because my laptop’s ports are just not cutting it anymore, and I’ve got to keep up with all these client video calls. The total on the receipt came to $620 — I mean, I don’t have a receipt anymore, but I do have the email confirmation from the vendor, which says it was shipped and paid for, and I’ve got the tracking info. I know you’re supposed to have a receipt, but I was in a rush when I got it, and I accidentally threw the paper one away — the digital copy is all I have now. It’s not like I bought a fancy laptop or anything, just a monitor and a dock, but the total was over $500, so I figured it’s probably not auto-approvable. Is it equipment? Because it’s hardware, right? I just don’t want to get flagged or rejected, and I really need this for work. I did not get a receipt, but I have the order history, and I’ve even attached the invoice from the vendor’s website. I don’t know if that counts — I’ve seen other people get approved with digital copies. But I’m just confused, because it’s over $500, so it can’t go to auto_approve, but I also don’t want to be sent to finance unless it’s absolutely necessary. Is this considered equipment? I mean, it’s not a laptop, but it’s not a small accessory either — it’s a monitor and a dock. The monitor’s got a serial number, and the dock too, so it’s not consumable. I don’t want to be penalized for losing a receipt, but I also don’t want to be in the wrong queue. I just need this approved so I can keep working efficiently.", "category": "equipment", "routing": "needs_manager", "rationale": "Hardware under $500 with a receipt routes to needs_manager, and hardware at or over $500 routes to needs_finance; however, missing a receipt routes to needs_manager regardless of amount, and this claim is for equipment with a total over $500 but no receipt, so it routes to needs_manager."}

{"description": "Hey, so I just got back from setting up the new client onboarding system at the downtown office, and I ended up needing to replace my old laptop since the screen kept flickering during video calls. I grabbed a brand-new 15-inch MacBook Pro with the M3 chip from the Apple Store — it’s got 16GB RAM, 1TB SSD, and all the latest ports. I didn’t get a receipt because I used my personal card for the purchase, but I took a photo of the Apple Store receipt on my phone and saved the email confirmation. The total came to $1,899, which is way over $500, and it’s clearly a piece of company hardware since it’s going to be used for client-facing work. I know it’s not a personal device, and I definitely didn’t buy it for fun — it’s for my job. Just hoping we can get this approved so I’m not stuck using an old laptop that’s barely functional.", "category": "equipment", "routing": "needs_finance", "rationale": "Hardware at or over $500 routes to needs_finance, and missing receipts place the claim in needs_manager, but since the amount exceeds $500, needs_finance takes precedence per the routing precedence rules."}

{"description": "Urgent request for approval on a $78.50 purchase of 10 high-capacity, 128GB USB flash drives from the company’s preferred vendor, ordered today to support an immediate sprint deadline for the new product launch. These are essential for deploying updated firmware and configuration files to 10 field engineers who are on-site at client locations with limited connectivity. The purchase was made via the company's bulk procurement portal, and the receipt is attached. While the total exceeds $75, each individual drive is under $50 and is clearly a consumable, non-serial, non-peripheral item used for temporary data transfer. No personal use is involved — all drives are branded with Meridian’s internal device provisioning tool and will be wiped and reused after the project. This is a single-item transaction, and the item qualifies as a small, non-serialized, consumable office supply. The urgency stems from the fact that the deployment cannot proceed without them, and the team has already been delayed by 4 hours.", "category": "office_supplies", "routing": "needs_manager", "rationale": "The purchase is for a single-item, consumable office supply under $50 with a receipt, but over $75 in total; since the item is not a serial-numbered accessory or hardware, and falls under the office_supplies category, it routes to needs_manager due to exceeding the $75 threshold."}

{"description": "Senior engineer submitting a claim for a $420 high-performance mechanical keyboard with a serial number, purchased from a vendor on a receipt dated three weeks ago. The keyboard was acquired to replace a faulty model that had been used for over two years and is essential for coding efficiency. It is not a consumable item, has a serial number, and is not part of a bundled purchase. The claim includes a receipt and is under $500. The employee is based in the U.S. and did not travel internationally or incur any related travel expenses, despite the purchase being made for work purposes.", "category": "equipment", "routing": "needs_manager", "rationale": "Hardware under $500 with a receipt routes to needs_manager, and this keyboard is equipment with a serial number, so it does not qualify as office_supplies."}

{"description": "Urgent: Need immediate approval for a $620 high-performance gaming monitor (model: LG UltraGear 32GK850F) purchased for a critical software development sprint — the current monitor is failing under heavy debugging loads and causing productivity loss. The monitor was ordered through the company’s bulk vendor portal, but the receipt was accidentally omitted during upload due to a system glitch in the procurement dashboard. I’ve attached the vendor order confirmation and invoice copy with the purchase details, including the total amount of $620. This is not a personal purchase — it's essential for maintaining development timelines and ensuring code stability. The unit has a serial number and is classified as hardware. I understand the receipt is missing, but this is a business-critical upgrade that cannot wait. Please prioritize this for immediate routing to finance for approval.", "category": "equipment", "routing": "needs_finance", "rationale": "Hardware at or over $500 routes to needs_finance, and bundled purchases are judged by the receipt total, which exceeds $500."}

{"description": "Project Manager submitted a claim for a high-performance mechanical keyboard and ergonomic mouse set totaling $580, purchased from a certified tech distributor. The keyboard is a 100% mechanical gaming model with programmable keys and RGB lighting; the mouse is a high-precision wireless model with a tactile scroll wheel. Both items are used exclusively for daily development work and were bought with a receipt. The total invoice amount exceeds $500, and the purchase was not bundled with any other items. The project manager has not previously claimed any similar equipment and is not on a recurring hardware replacement cycle.", "category": "equipment", "routing": "needs_finance", "rationale": "Hardware at or over $500 routes to needs_finance, and bundled purchases are judged by the receipt total, not per item, which applies here as the total exceeds $500."}

{"description": "Urgent: I need to submit this for reimbursement immediately—just bought a $42 USB-C charging cable for my work laptop, which is on a critical client site in Seattle. The cable was damaged during transit and I had to replace it on the spot because my laptop wouldn’t charge. I only have the receipt from the local electronics store, which I scanned and attached. It’s a small, consumable accessory under $50, and I’m in a rush to get back on the road before the next meeting. I know it’s not a major item, but the company device is now unusable without it. I can’t wait another day—this is time-sensitive and purely for work purposes. Please process this as soon as possible.", "category": "office_supplies", "routing": "auto_approve", "rationale": "The claim is for a consumable accessory under $50 with a receipt, under $75, and falls under office_supplies, satisfying all three conditions for auto-approval."}

{"description": "I submitted a claim for a $420 ergonomic keyboard for my home office setup, which I use daily for team events and client calls. I thought since it's for work and we're doing a team event this week, it might qualify as a team tool. But I'm not sure if it's equipment or office supplies — it's not a laptop, but it's not exactly a pen or paper either. The receipt is attached, and I just want to make sure I'm not breaking policy by calling it office supplies when it's really a peripheral that's been used for the last three team events.", "category": "equipment", "routing": "needs_manager", "rationale": "Hardware under $500 with a receipt routes to needs_manager, and the keyboard qualifies as equipment despite being used for team events, per the equipment definition and routing rules."}

{"description": "As part of a remote work infrastructure upgrade, I purchased a 27-inch 4K monitor for my home office setup to support dual-screen workflows during client calls and financial modeling tasks. The device was ordered through the company's approved vendor portal, but due to a temporary system outage during checkout, the receipt was not generated and transmitted to the expense system. The total cost was $395, well under $500. The monitor has a serial number and is not a consumable item; it qualifies as hardware per the equipment definition in the software policy. Although the transaction was initiated for business use, the receipt is missing, which triggers the 'missing receipt' rule from the routing policy.", "category": "equipment", "routing": "needs_manager", "rationale": "Hardware under $500 without a receipt routes to needs_manager, as per the expense policy's routing rules and the equipment section of the software policy."}

{
  "description": "Hi, I’m not sure if I did this right—so I’m submitting this claim for a networking event I attended last Friday night with the team to meet potential clients from a new startup we’re trying to onboard. We all went to a fancy rooftop bar downtown, and the total bill came to $380 for 6 people, including a couple of drinks, some appetizers, and a couple of shared small plates. I didn’t realize at the time that the event was officially called a 'client engagement cocktail hour,' but the client was there—her name was on the receipt, and she was seated at our table. The receipt shows the client’s name and the business name of the bar, and the total includes a $120 charge for three glasses of champagne and two cocktails. I attached the receipt and filled out the expense form, but I’m confused because I thought it was just a team dinner. But since a client was present, I think it’s supposed to be client_entertainment? Also, the total is over $150, and there were more than three people. Should this go to finance? Or is it still meals? I wasn’t sure if I needed to categorize it as client_entertainment even though the event wasn’t a formal meeting—it was more of a hangout, but the client was definitely there and we were trying to build rapport. I just want to make sure I didn’t mess up the policy.",
  "category": "client_entertainment",
  "routing": "needs_finance",
  "rationale": "Since a client was present at the event and the total exceeds $150, the claim is classified as client_entertainment and routed to needs_finance per the routing policy."

{"description": "As a remote worker based in Portland, I purchased a new ergonomic standing desk to improve my home office setup during extended work hours. The desk was ordered from a commercial retailer with a receipt, and the total invoice amount came to $485. Although I use the desk primarily for work, I also use it occasionally for personal tasks such as online course work and remote family video calls. The desk has a serial number and is not consumable in nature, which disqualifies it from being categorized as an office supply. Given its nature as a hardware component with a fixed form and durable function, it falls under the equipment category per company policy. The total cost is under $500, but since it is not a consumable item and has a serial number, it cannot be auto-approved or routed to auto_approve. Furthermore, it is not a recurring expense or related to software, travel, meals, or client entertainment.", "category": "equipment", "routing": "needs_manager", "rationale": "Hardware under $500 with a receipt routes to needs_manager, and items with a serial number are classified as equipment, not office supplies, per the Equipment section of the Software & Equipment Purchasing Policy."}

{"description": "Urgent bulk order of office supplies for the new Austin office launch—need 200 high-capacity printer cartridges, 500 reams of eco-friendly paper, and 1,000 custom branded pens. The total comes to $320, with a receipt attached, all items are consumables under $50 each, and the purchase was made via company account through a verified vendor. The order was processed last week but delayed due to shipping carrier issues—no invoice was attached at time of submission, but the receipt confirms all items were delivered and received by the office manager. This is a critical need to support team onboarding and client-facing operations starting next Monday.", "category": "office_supplies", "routing": "needs_manager", "rationale": "The claim involves office supplies totaling $320 (under $500) with a receipt attached, which routes to needs_manager per the routing policy, as office supplies are not eligible for auto-approval even if under $75."}
